mainTopic: How a person's status as a כהן or לוי is established: by public signs like נשיאות כפים, reading first in shul, or receiving תרומה, and by the word of a relative such as a father or brother.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an answer about חלה: not all of the Jews went up to ארץ ישראל in the days of עזרא. Next, the גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that נשיאות כפים makes someone a כהן even for יוחסין, because the ברייתא lists it next to עדות. The proof is pushed back: the ברייתא means a witness who reports a חזקה he saw, and that testimony is only as strong as the חזקה. Stories show this kind of testimony. רבי אמי accepts a man as a כהן because a witness saw him read first with a לוי after him, and רבי יהושע בן לוי accepts a man as a לוי because he read right after a כהן. Before ריש לקיש, a witness says a man read first, but ריש לקיש wants to know whether he received תרומה at the threshing floor. רבי אלעזר, and later רבי יוחנן himself, answer that כהונה does not stop where there is no threshing floor. Then the גמרא works out that רבי trusted a father about his son's כהונה, at least for eating תרומה, and רבי חייא trusted a brother about his brother being a לוי. The amud ends by asking רבי חייא why a brother is believed when a father is not, since both are relatives.

steps.title: Not everyone went up in the days of עזרא
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous answer: not all of the Jews returned to ארץ ישראל, so the Torah-level obligation of חלה did not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not all of them went up.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the previous discussion about חלה. The גמרא is finishing its answer: in the days of עזרא, not all of the Jews came up to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah obligation of חלה depends on all of the Jews being in the land. Since most of them stayed in בבל, חלה in the time of עזרא was only a rabbinic obligation, and so it cannot help prove anything about the Torah-level law.

phrases.english: Not all of them went up.
phrases.notes: He means went up to ארץ ישראל with עזרא. Most of the people stayed behind in בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the previous section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual limitation: the condition for a Torah obligation was not met.
steps.terutzMaskana: חלה in the days of עזרא was rabbinic, because not all of the Jews returned.

steps.title: A ברייתא listing three ways to establish כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a חזקה of כהונה comes from נשיאות כפים, from sharing in תרומה at the threshing floors, and from עדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A presumption of being a כהן comes from lifting the hands (to bless the people), from the sharing out at the threshing floors, and from testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to answer its question by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the actual proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open question is whether נשיאות כפים proves a person is a כהן even for יוחסין. The ברייתא lists נשיאות כפים together with עדות, and that pairing is what the גמרא will try to use as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an opening that brings a source as a proof
The lifting of the hands: the כהנים blessing the people
The sharing out of תרומה at the threshing floors

phrases.english: Come and hear: A presumption of being a priest comes from:
Lifting of the hands, and the sharing out at the threshing floors,
phrases.notes: Seeing someone receive a share of תרומה at the threshing floor shows that people treat him as a כהן.

phrases.english: And testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new proof attempt for the main question about נשיאות כפים.
steps.raayaObject: Whether נשיאות כפים creates a חזקה for יוחסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists נשיאות כפים next to עדות.

steps.title: Is testimony just a presumption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא calls עדות a 'חזקה,' since testimony is much stronger than a presumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is testimony a presumption?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that something sounds wrong in the ברייתא's wording. Testimony is full proof, so why list it as a mere presumption?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is a status built on how a person is treated. עדות is direct proof from witnesses. Putting the two in the same list seems odd, and this sets up a new way of reading the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is testimony a presumption? (meaning: of course not; it is stronger)

phrases.english: Is testimony a presumption?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא listing עדות as a kind of חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Testimony is full proof, not just a presumption, so the list does not make sense as written.

steps.title: Reading it as: נשיאות כפים is like עדות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means that נשיאות כפים is as strong as עדות, so it works even for יוחסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it means: lifting of the hands is like testimony. Just as testimony works for lineage, so too lifting of the hands works for lineage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own wording problem with a new reading, and that reading proves the point it was looking for: נשיאות כפים counts for יוחסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'and testimony' really means 'like testimony,' then the ברייתא is making נשיאות כפים equal to עדות. Since עדות is good enough for lineage and marriage, נשיאות כפים would be too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that...: introduces the reading the גמרא is pushing for
This is what it is saying
Just as... so too...: a comparison

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what it is saying:
Lifting of the hands is like testimony:
Just as testimony works for lineage,
So too lifting of the hands works for lineage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the wording problem from step 3 in a way that proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: נשיאות כפים establishes כהונה for יוחסין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading the ברייתא as comparing נשיאות כפים to עדות.

steps.title: No: testimony based on a presumption
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא means a testimony that is built on a חזקה, and such testimony is only as strong as that חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No: testimony that comes from the strength of a presumption is like the presumption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by giving a different reading of 'testimony' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עדות in the list is not regular eyewitness proof of lineage. It is a witness reporting a חזקה he saw, so it can only be as strong as that חזקה. With this reading, the ברייתא no longer proves that נשיאות כפים works for יוחסין.

keyTerms.meaning: That comes from the strength of
Like its presumption: the same strength as the חזקה it is based on

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean testimony is weak in general. It is only talking about a witness whose testimony is itself based on what he saw people do, which is a חזקה.

phrases.english: No: testimony that comes from the strength of a presumption
Is like its presumption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא only. The main question is not decided.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's 'testimony' can mean testimony based on a חזקה, so it does not need to mean 'נשיאות כפים is like עדות'.

steps.title: רבי אמי's case: he read first
steps.stepSummary: To show what testimony based on a חזקה looks like, the גמרא tells of a man who told רבי אמי that someone was a כהן because he saw him read first in shul.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case of a certain man who came before רבי אמי and said to him: I hold a presumption about this man that he is a כהן. He said to him: What did you see? He said to him: That he read first in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that illustrates the 'testimony based on a presumption' from step 5. Here the witness explains what he saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness did not see the man's lineage. He only saw him treated as a כהן by being called first to the Torah. That is exactly testimony that comes from a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold a presumption: I know of an established status

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: As in the case of a certain man who came before Rabbi Ami,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּחְזְקַנִי בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא כֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: He said to him: I know this man has the status of a priest.
He said to him: What did you see?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֶׁקָּרָא רִאשׁוֹן בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת.
phrases.english: He said to him: That he read first in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the 'testimony based on a presumption' from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Testimony based on a חזקה is accepted.

steps.title: Was he called as a כהן or as a great man?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks whether the man was called first because he was a כהן, or because he was an important person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it because he was presumed to be a כהן, or because he was presumed to be a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי checks whether the witness's evidence really proves anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being called first could happen for two different reasons: being a כהן, or being an important תלמיד חכם. If it was for importance, it says nothing about כהונה.

phrases.english: Was it on the presumption that he is a priest,
Or on the presumption that he is a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁהוּא כֹּהֵן, אוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the evidence given in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether reading first shows כהונה or just importance.

steps.title: A לוי read after him, so רבי אמי accepts him
steps.stepSummary: The witness answers that a לוי read right after him, which shows he was called as a כהן. רבי אמי accepts him as a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a לוי read after him. And רבי אמי raised him to כהונה based on his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The witness gives the detail that settles רבי אמי's doubt, and רבי אמי rules that the man is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לוי is called second only when a כהן was called first. So the order of the readings shows that the first reader was treated as a כהן, and that was enough for רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: And he raised him (to a status)

phrases.english: That a Levite read after him.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶעֱלָהוּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי לִכְהוּנָּה עַל פִּיו.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami raised him to the priesthood based on his word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A לוי read next, which shows he was called as a כהן.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי's case: he read second
steps.stepSummary: A similar case: a man told רבי יהושע בן לוי that someone was a לוי because he saw him read second in shul.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי יהושע בן לוי and said to him: I hold a presumption about this man that he is a לוי. He said to him: What did you see? He said to him: That he read second in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching story, this time about establishing someone as a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as before: the witness reports only what he saw in shul, which is testimony built on a חזקה. Now the reading being used is the second one.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּחְזְקַנִי בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא לֵוִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I know this man has the status of a Levite.
He said to him: What did you see?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שֶׁקָּרָא שֵׁנִי בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת.
phrases.english: He said to him: That he read second in the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example that matches the case of רבי אמי.
steps.raayaObject: Testimony based on a חזקה is accepted for לויה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: Was he called as a לוי or as a great man?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks whether the man read second because he was a לוי, or because he was an important person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it because he was presumed to be a לוי, or because he was presumed to be a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי tests the evidence, the same way רבי אמי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no כהן was there, people could be called by how important they are. In that case reading second would not prove the man is a לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The presumption of being a Levite

phrases.english: Was it on the presumption that he is a Levite,
Or on the presumption that he is a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁהוּא לֵוִי, אוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the evidence given in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether reading second shows לויה or just importance.

steps.title: A כהן read before him, so he is accepted as a לוי
steps.stepSummary: The witness answers that a כהן read right before him, which shows he was called as a לוי. רבי יהושע בן לוי accepts him as a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a כהן read before him. And רבי יהושע בן לוי raised him to the status of a לוי based on his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The witness gives the deciding detail, and רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the man is a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading right after a כהן is the spot kept for a לוי, so the order proves how he was treated. Both stories show a בית דין accepting a witness who reports a חזקה he saw, as long as the details really point to that status.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא was pushed back: its 'testimony' can mean a witness reporting a חזקה he saw. The stories of רבי אמי and רבי יהושע בן לוי show this kind of testimony, built on the order of the Torah readings: a לוי after him proves he is a כהן, and a כהן before him proves he is a לוי.

phrases.english: That a priest read before him.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַעֲלֵהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִלְוִיָּה עַל פִּיו.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raised him to Levite status based on his word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10 and closes the second story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כהן read just before him, which shows he was called as a לוי.

steps.title: A man testifies before ריש לקיש that someone is a כהן
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a man comes to ריש לקיש and says that someone has an established status as a כהן in his eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before ריש לקיש and said: I know this man to be a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story about testifying that someone is a כהן. This line just sets up the case; the questions come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier stories with רבי אמי and רבי יהושע בן לוי, someone testifies about another person's status. The witness is not saying he knows the family tree, only that this man is treated as a כהן. The next steps will check what that treatment actually was.

keyTerms.meaning: A great אמורא of ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
I hold him as established (I know him to have this status)
An established status that we rely on

phrases.english: A certain man who came before Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מוּחְזְקַנִי בָּזֶה שֶׁהוּא כֹּהֵן.
phrases.english: said to him: This man is established to me as a kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story on the same theme as the stories of רבי אמי and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.raayaObject: What kind of evidence is enough to establish someone as a כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story that came before ריש לקיש

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks what the witness saw
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks the witness what he saw that made him think the man is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: What did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks the witness to explain his claim. He wants to know exactly what the man was seen doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "he is a כהן" is only a conclusion. A judge needs the actual facts behind it. Only then can he decide whether those facts really prove כהונה.

phrases.english: He said to him: What did you see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the testimony given in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What act the witness saw that made him treat the man as a כהן

steps.title: The witness saw him read first in shul
steps.stepSummary: The witness answers that the man was called up first to the Torah reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: I saw that he read first in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The witness gives his evidence: the man got the first עליה. That is normally the כהן's עליה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of evidence used in the earlier stories. Being called first in shul is a public sign that the community treats him as a כהן. The question is whether ריש לקיש will accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Read first, got the first עליה to the Torah

phrases.english: [He said to him:] That he read first
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them. Here the witness is answering.

phrases.english: in the synagogue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw the man get the first עליה in shul.

steps.title: ריש לקיש demands proof from the threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש is not satisfied with reading first. He asks if the witness saw the man receive תרומה at the threshing floors.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Did you see him receive a share of תרומה at the threshing floors?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on the evidence. To him, only receiving תרומה proves someone is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's view is that reading first is not strong enough. The real sign of a כהן is getting תרומה when it is handed out at the threshing floor. So he challenges whether the witness's evidence counts at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floors, where grain was processed and תרומה given out
The gift of produce given to a כהן, which only a כהן may eat

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רְאִיתִיו שֶׁחִילֵּק עַל הַגֳּרָנוֹת?
phrases.english: He said to him: Did you see him receive a share at the threshing floors?
phrases.notes: He means a share of תרומה, which was handed out to כהנים at the threshing floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the evidence given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that reading first in shul proves כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only receiving תרומה at the threshing floor proves someone is a כהן; reading first is not enough.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: no threshing floor does not end the כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers ריש לקיש: if there is no threshing floor in the place, does כהונה just disappear?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to him: And if there is no threshing floor there, has the כהונה stopped?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר rejects ריש לקיש's demand. Reading first is enough, because there won't always be a threshing floor to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a place with no threshing floor, nobody gives out תרומה. If that were the only proof, no one there could ever be proven a כהן. That makes no sense, so reading first must also count.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם גּוֹרֶן, בָּטְלָה כְּהוּנָּה?
phrases.english: And if there is no threshing floor there, has the priesthood ceased?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם גּוֹרֶן, בָּטְלָה כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ריש לקיש's demand in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's claim that only תרומה at the threshing floor proves כהונה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There are places with no threshing floor, and כהונה cannot depend on that.

steps.title: The same case comes before רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Another time, ריש לקיש and רבי אלעזר were sitting before רבי יוחנן, and a similar case came up. ריש לקיש asks the same question again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were sitting before רבי יוחנן, and a case like this came before him. ריש לקיש said to the witness: Did you see him receive a share at the threshing floor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with the same kind of case. This sets up רבי יוחנן's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש still holds his view from before. He asks the exact same question about the threshing floor. Now the answer will come from רבי יוחנן himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל, teacher of רבי אלעזר

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Once they were sitting before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
phrases.notes: "They" means ריש לקיש and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: a case like this came before him.
Reish Lakish said to him:
Did you see him receive a share at the threshing floor?

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the scene of steps 12-15, now in front of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: Whether reading first is enough to prove כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second case that came before רבי יוחנן

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives the same answer as רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש with the very same words: if there is no threshing floor, does כהונה stop?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: And if there is no threshing floor there, has the כהונה stopped?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's demand, using exactly the words רבי אלעזר had used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words match word for word. This shows that רבי אלעזר's answer was really רבי יוחנן's teaching. It also confirms that reading first is accepted as proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם גּוֹרֶן, בָּטְלָה כְּהוּנָּה?
phrases.english: And if there is no threshing floor there, has the priesthood ceased?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְאִם אֵין שָׁם גּוֹרֶן, בָּטְלָה כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ריש לקיש's question in step 17, matching רבי אלעזר's words in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's demand for proof from the threshing floor
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כהונה cannot depend on there being a threshing floor.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is upset that רבי אלעזר did not quote רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש looks at רבי אלעזר sharply and complains that he heard this from רבי יוחנן but did not say it in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש turned and looked at רבי אלעזר harshly. He said: You heard this from רבי יוחנן, and you did not tell it to us in his name?
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with ריש לקיש realizing the answer came from רבי יוחנן. He complains that רבי אלעזר hid the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When רבי אלעזר said it alone, ריש לקיש did not accept it. Once he saw it was רבי יוחנן's teaching, it carried much more weight. The point of the story: the ruling that reading first proves כהונה is רבי יוחנן's.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of the blacksmith, a nickname for רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: Reading first in shul is enough to establish someone as a כהן. This is the view of רבי יוחנן, said first by his student רבי אלעזר, against ריש לקיש who wanted proof from תרומה.

phrases.english: He turned and looked at Rabbi Elazar harshly,
he said: You heard the words of bar Nappaḥa,
phrases.notes: בר נפחא is a nickname for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: and you did not say them to us in his name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by linking רבי אלעזר's answer (step 16) to רבי יוחנן (step 18).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling that reading first proves כהונה comes from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי and רבי חייא: trusting a father or a brother
steps.stepSummary: Of רבי and רבי חייא, one accepted a son as a כהן based on his father's word, and one accepted a brother as a לוי based on his brother's word. We are not told who did which.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי and רבי חייא: one raised a son to כהונה based on his father's word, and the other raised a brother to לויה based on his brother's word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new report about two great rabbis. It does not say which rabbi did which, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is whether a close relative can be trusted about family status. In one case a father vouched for his son, in the other a brother vouched for his brother. The גמרא will now try to match each case to the right rabbi.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה
The status of being a לוי

phrases.english: Rabbi and Rabbi Ḥiyya,

phrases.aramaic: חַד הֶעֱלָה בֵּן עַל פִּי אָבִיו לִכְהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: one raised a son to the priesthood based on his father's word,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד הֶעֱלָה אָח עַל פִּי אָחִיו לִלְוִיָּה.
phrases.english: and one raised a brother to Levite status based on his brother's word.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא, חַד הֶעֱלָה בֵּן עַל פִּי אָבִיו לִכְהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: trusting relatives about status, instead of public signs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One of them trusted a father about his son's כהונה; the other trusted a brother about his brother's לויה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי trusted the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a ברייתא that רבי is the one who trusted a father about his son. In the ברייתא, רבי says the father is believed to let his son eat תרומה, but not to marry him to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי is the one who raised a son to כהונה based on his father, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone came and said, "This is my son, and he is a כהן," he is believed to let him eat תרומה, but not believed to marry him to a woman. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer "who did which" from step 20. It brings a ברייתא where רבי trusts a father about his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי believes the father enough for eating תרומה. That fits the story of trusting a father about כהונה, so רבי is the one who did it. רבי still limits it: the father is not believed for marriage, which is about family lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: To marry him to a woman (of pure lineage)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not fully trust the father. He trusts him only for eating תרומה, not for marriage. The proof works just because he trusts the father for something.

phrases.english: It may be concluded that Rabbi raised a son
to the priesthood based on his father's word,
as it is taught: If one came and said:
This is my son, and he is a priest —
he is believed to let him eat teruma,
but he is not believed to marry him to a woman,
phrases.notes: He means a woman who may only marry someone of pure lineage, since that depends on family status.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי הֶעֱלָה בֵּן עַל פִּי אָבִיו לִכְהוּנָּה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to identify which rabbi did which case in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי is the one who trusted a father about his son's כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי believes a father to let his son eat תרומה

steps.title: רבי חייא: believe him for both or for neither
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי חייא argues with רבי: if you trust the father for תרומה, trust him for marriage too; if not for marriage, then not for תרומה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to him: If you believe him to let his son eat תרומה, believe him to marry him to a woman. And if you do not believe him to marry him to a woman, do not believe him to let him eat תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא challenges רבי's split ruling inside the ברייתא. He says it makes no sense to trust the father halfway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gave the father partial trust: yes for תרומה, no for marriage. רבי חייא attacks that split: either the father is trusted or he is not. This also hints that רבי חייא does not trust a father here, so he is likely the one who trusted the brother.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument shows the two rabbis truly differ about trusting a father. That supports the גמרא's claim that רבי, not רבי חייא, is the one who raised a son to כהונה through his father.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him:
If you believe him to let him eat teruma —
believe him to marry him to a woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִי אַתָּה מַאֲמִינוֹ לְהַשִּׂיאוֹ אִשָּׁה —
phrases.english: And if you do not believe him to marry him to a woman —
do not believe him for eating teruma!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: אִם אַתָּה מַאֲמִינוֹ לְהַאֲכִילוֹ בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's ruling in the ברייתא brought in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the father is believed for תרומה but not for marriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trust cannot be split: the father should be believed for both matters or for neither.

steps.title: רבי explains why the father is trusted for תרומה but not for marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers רבי חייא's challenge from Step 22. The father is believed about תרומה because that is in his power. He is not believed about marriage because that is not in his power.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: I trust the father to let his son eat תרומה, since it is in his power to feed him תרומה. But I do not trust him to marry his son to a woman, since it is not in his power to marry him to a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי is answering רבי חייא's 'all or nothing' challenge. He explains why he splits the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא said that a father must be trusted either for both things or for neither. רבי answers that the two cases are different. A person is believed about something he can already do on his own. Feeding his son תרומה is in the father's hands, but marrying the son to a woman of pure lineage is not.

keyTerms.meaning: I believe him / I trust his word
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים may eat
In his hand, meaning something within his power
To marry him off to a woman

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying the father is a liar about marriage. He is saying the father's word only carries power in an area the father already controls.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי answering רבי חייא inside the same ברייתא.

phrases.english: I trust him to let him eat terumah
since it is in his power to feed him terumah,
but I do not trust him to marry him to a woman
since it is not in his power to marry him to a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי מַאֲמִינוֹ לְהַאֲכִילוֹ בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא's challenge from Step 22 inside the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the two cases: what is in his power versus what is not in his power
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Trust should be all or nothing: if the father is believed for תרומה, he should be believed for marriage too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A father is believed only about what is within his power. Feeding his son תרומה is in his power, but marrying him off is not.

steps.title: Proven: רבי trusted the father, so רבי חייא trusted the brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא proves רבי is the one who trusted a father about his son. That leaves רבי חייא as the one who trusted a brother about his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is proven. And since רבי accepted a son as a כהן based on his father's word, רבי חייא is the one who accepted a brother as a לוי based on his brother's word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes its proof from Step 21. Now that we know which case was רבי's, it works out that the other case belongs to רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 told us that each of the two rulings belonged to one of these sages, but not which one. The ברייתא shows that רבי trusted a father about his son. So the remaining ruling, trusting a brother about his brother, must be רבי חייא's.

keyTerms.meaning: It is proven / we can conclude
Raised up, meaning he gave the person a status of יחוס

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: a father is believed about his son for כהונה, at least for eating תרומה. רבי חייא: a brother is believed about his brother for being a לוי.

phrases.english: It is proven.
And since Rabbi raised up a son
phrases.notes: 'Raised up' means he gave the person that status and accepted him as a כהן or לוי.

phrases.english: to the priesthood based on his father's word
Rabbi Chiya raised up a brother
to Levite status based on his brother's word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof begun in Step 21 and assigns the remaining ruling from Step 20 to רבי חייא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי is the one who trusted a father about his son. רבי חייא is the one who trusted a brother about his brother.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי חייא: a brother is also a relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חייא. He does not trust a father about his son because they are relatives, yet a brother is also a relative of his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חייא, what is the difference? A son, about whom the father is not believed because he is a relative of his father? A brother is also a relative of his brother!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has assigned the brother ruling to רבי חייא, it asks how his two positions fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי חייא did not trust the father, and the גמרא assumes the reason is that relatives cannot testify for each other. But רבי חייא did trust a brother about his brother, and a brother is just as much a relative. So he should either accept both or reject both.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking for a distinction between two cases)
A relative, who is normally not allowed to testify for family

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya, what is different
a son, that [the father is] not [believed],
because he is a relative of his father

phrases.aramaic: אָח נָמֵי קָרוֹב הוּא אֵצֶל אָחִיו?!
phrases.english: a brother too is a relative of his brother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of Step 24 to point out an apparent contradiction within רבי חייא's own positions.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's two positions: he does not trust a father about his son, yet he trusts a brother about his brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the problem with the father is that he is a relative, the brother has the very same problem, so רבי חייא should treat both cases alike.
